topic: Decoding Epidemics: The Mechanics of the SIR Model
target_audience: University students (Introductory STEM or Public Health)

sections.title: Introduction: Why Do We Model Outbreaks?
lecture_lines: Epidemics spread through susceptible populations rapidly.
One spark ignites a wildfire of infection.
We must predict the outbreak's peak impact.
animations: Show population nodes with '#FFFFFF' label 'Healthy' using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg].
Visualize connection lines spreading between nodes.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Population Dynamics & Rates
lecture_lines: Epidemics involve movement between distinct population states.
Rates determine how fast transitions occur daily.
Think of flow filling an epidemic bucket.
animations: Animate growth rate curve using '#00FF00' alongside a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bucket.svg] to represent resource accumulation.
Show population cap with dashed '#FFFF00' line.

sections.title: The SIR Framework: Defining the States
lecture_lines: SIR defines three key population states.
Susceptible people haven't been infected yet.
Infected individuals are currently spreading the virus.
Recovered individuals are now immune to reinfection.
These states track the entire disease progression.
animations: Display Susceptible(S) block in '#0000FF' with icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg].
Display Infected(I) block in '#FF0000' with icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/virus.svg].
Display Recovered(R) block in '#00FF00' with icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg].
Animate transition arrows between S, I, and R.
Label all states clearly with '#FFFFFF' text.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics: The Transition Equations
lecture_lines: Transmission happens through interactions between populations.
Infections occur as susceptible meet infected individuals.
Recovery flows from infected to removed states.
We model these using differential transition equations.
Equations show how infection and recovery change.
animations: Write dS/dt equation in '#FFFFFF' on screen, showing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg] transitioning to infection.
Write dI/dt equation in '#FFFFFF' on screen with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microbe.svg] appearing.
Write dR/dt equation in '#FFFFFF' on screen, showing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hospital.svg] in the background.
Highlight infection term (βSI/N) with '#FF0000' flash next to [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microbe.svg].
Highlight recovery term (γI) with '#00FF00' flash next to [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/syringe.svg].

sections.title: Simulation & Application: 'Flattening the Curve'
lecture_lines: Adjusting transmission variables can flatten curves.
Social distancing reduces the infection peak significantly.
Predictive models guide effective public health policy.
animations: Animate infection peak rise with '#FF0000' among a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg] population.
Show 'Social Distancing' intervention effect on curve using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg] icons to represent distancing.
Observe flattened infection curve in '#00FF00' as the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg] units stabilize.
